units.en: Han had held off Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north. He had to be won by conciliation, not crushed by force. In the end he brought the region back to the empire. Was that not wise policy?
units.literal: Moreover Han resisted Zhenjie in the south and defeated Xiancheng in the north; he should have been won by kindness and could not be subdued by force; in the end he caused the region to return to the state — was this not a sound plan?

units.zh: 向討之，即為劇賊矣。
units.en: Had the court attacked him instead, he would have become a far more dangerous rebel.
units.literal: Had they attacked him instead, he would have become a fierce bandit.

units.zh: 然事佛僥福，朋勢取容，非君子之道焉。
units.en: Yet in seeking fortune through Buddhism and currying favor through factions he fell short of the way of a true gentleman.
units.literal: Yet in serving Buddhism to seek fortune and currying favor through factional power he did not follow the way of the gentleman.

units.zh: 贊曰：玄宗失德，祿山肆逆。
units.en: The encomium reads: Xuanzong lost his virtue, and An Lushan rose in rebellion.
units.literal: The encomium says: Xuanzong lost virtue and Lushan wildly rebelled.

units.zh: 見素竭節，諸公協力。
units.en: Jiansu gave his utmost, and these men worked together in the state's service.
units.literal: Jiansu exhausted his integrity and the various lords joined their strength.

units.zh: 肅宗立，命與房琯、韋見素赴行在所，帝為製遺愛碑於蜀以寵之。
units.en: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Yuan was ordered to join Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu at the mobile court; the emperor had a stele of enduring favor carved in Shu to honor him.
units.literal: When Emperor Suzong was established, he was ordered to go with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to the mobile court; the Emperor had an "Inscribed Stele of Enduring Favor" made in Shu to honor him.

units.zh: 侍中裴耀卿、中書令張九齡、禮部尚書李林甫等奏曰：「外族之親，禮無厭降。
units.en: Chief Attendant Pei Yaoqing, Grand Counselor Zhang Jiuling, Minister of Rites Li Linfu, and others wrote: "External kin are not subject to ritual demotion.
units.literal: Attendant-in-chief Pei Yaoqing, Grand Counselor Zhang Jiuling, Minister of Rites Li Linfu, and others memorialized, saying: "Kin of the external clan—in ritual there is no suppressed demotion.

units.zh: 外甥既為舅母制服，舅母還合報之。
units.en: A nephew already mourns his aunt by marriage; she in turn should return the obligation.
units.literal: The sister's son already wears mourning for the mother's brother's wife; the mother's brother's wife in turn ought to return it.

units.zh: 夫外甥既為報服，則與夫之姨舅，以類是同，外甥之妻，不得無服。
units.en: If a nephew wears return mourning, the same logic covers the husband's aunts and uncles; a nephew's wife cannot go without dress.
units.literal: Since the sister's son already wears return mourning, then with the husband's mother's brothers and sisters it is the same by category; the sister's son's wife cannot be without mourning.

units.zh: 所增者頗廣，所引者漸疏。
units.en: What is added grows wide; what is cited grows remote.
units.literal: What is added is rather broad; what is cited grows ever more distant.

units.zh: 微臣愚蒙，猶有未達。」
units.en: We, foolish and ignorant petty officials, still do not fully grasp it."
units.literal: We, foolish and ignorant petty officials, still do not fully grasp it."

units.zh: ○苗晉卿裴冕裴遵慶子向向子寅寅子樞=苗晉卿=苗晉卿，上黨壺關人。
units.en: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's son Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
units.literal: [Section:] Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, Pei Zunqing, his son Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, Yin's son Shu. = Miao Jinqing = Miao Jinqing was a native of Huguan in Shangdang.

units.zh: 父殆庶，官至絳州龍門縣丞，早卒，以晉卿贈太子少保。
units.en: His father Dai-shu rose only to assistant magistrate of Longmen in Jiang prefecture and died young; on account of Jinqing's eminence he was posthumously granted the title Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His father Dai-shu, reached office as Assistant Magistrate of Longmen County in Jiang Prefecture, died early; because of Jinqing he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 晉卿幼好學，善屬文，進士擢第。
units.en: Jinqing had loved study from childhood, wrote well, and passed the jinshi civil examination.
units.literal: Jinqing from youth loved learning, excelled at literary composition, and was selected in the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 太常議謚曰「懿獻」。
units.en: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices proposed the posthumous name Yi-xian ("Reverent and Dedicated").
units.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices deliberated and gave the posthumous title "Yi-xian."

units.zh: 至是載為中書侍郎、平章事，懷舊恩，諷有司改謚曰文貞。
units.en: By then Yuan Zai was vice director of the Secretariat and chief minister; remembering old kindness, he prompted the authorities to change the posthumous name to Wen-zhen ("Cultured and Upright").
units.literal: By this time Zai was Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-ordinating Minister; cherishing old grace, he hinted to the responsible offices to change the posthumous title to Wen-zhen.

units.zh: 遷侍御史，歷度支、兵、吏部三員外郎。
units.en: He rose to attending censor and then held vice-director posts in the revenue, war, and personnel ministries in turn.
units.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and served successively as Vice Director in the ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel.

units.zh: 會肅宗至鳳翔，手詔追晉卿赴行在，即日拜為左相，軍國大務悉以咨之。
units.en: When Suzong reached Fengxiang he sent a personal summons for Jinqing to join the mobile court and that same day named him left chancellor, consulting him on every major civil and military matter.
units.literal: When Suzong reached Fengxiang, by autograph edict he recalled Jinqing to the mobile court; that very day he was appointed Left Chancellor, and all great military and state affairs were entirely consulted with him.

units.zh: 既收兩京，以功封韓國公，食實封五百戶，改為侍中。
units.en: After the two capitals were retaken he was enfeoffed Duke of Han with five hundred taxable households and promoted to palace attendant.
units.literal: Having recovered the two capitals, because of merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Han state, with substantive fief of five hundred households, and changed to Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 前後典選五年，政既寬弛，胥吏多因緣為奸，賄賂大行。
units.en: He oversaw the examinations for five years in all; his rule was lenient and slack, so clerks seized every opening for graft and bribes became rampant.
units.literal: Over five years before and after in charge of selection, because administration was already lax, clerks often took advantage to commit wrongdoing, and bribery flourished greatly.

units.zh: 天寶三載閏二月，轉魏郡太守，充河北采訪處置使，居職三年，政化洽聞。
units.en: In the intercalary second month of Tianbao 3 he became prefect of Wei and Hebei investigating commissioner; after three years his administration was celebrated throughout the region.
units.literal: In the intercalary second month of the third year of Tianbao, he was transferred to Prefect of Wei commandery, serving as Hebei Investigating and Disposing Commissioner; in office three years, his government and transformation were harmoniously heard of.

units.zh: 世以儒素稱。
units.en: His lineage was known for upright Confucian learning and modest living.
units.literal: His family for generations was famed for Confucian simplicity.

units.zh: 開元二十三年，遷吏部郎中。
units.en: In Kaiyuan 23 (735), he was made a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 二十四年，與吏部郎中孫逖並拜中書舍人。
units.en: The next year he and Sun Ti of the personnel ministry were both promoted to drafter in the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, together with Sun Ti, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he was jointly appointed Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 二十七年，以本官權知吏部選事。
units.en: In Kaiyuan 27 he was given his existing rank but charged with directing the ministry's selection examinations.
units.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, with his existing office he was temporarily put in charge of personnel selection matters.

units.zh: 二十九年，拜吏部侍郎。
units.en: In Kaiyuan 29 he was made vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 天寶二年春，御史中丞張倚男奭參選，晉卿與遙以倚初承恩，欲悅附之，考選人判等凡六十四人，分甲乙丙科，奭在其首。
units.en: In the spring of Tianbao 2 (743), Zhang Yi's son Shi entered the examinations. Jinqing and Yao, eager to curry favor with the newly favored Zhang Yi, ranked sixty-four candidates in three tiers and placed Shi at the top.
units.literal: In spring of the second year of Tianbao, Zhang Yi, Vice Censor-in-Chief, his son Shi participated in selection; Jinqing and Yao because Yi had newly received favor wished to please and attach to him—they evaluated candidates' written grades totaling sixty-four persons, dividing into First, Second, and Third classes, with Shi at their head.

units.zh: 屬祿山叛逆，楊國忠以晉卿有時望，將抑之，乃奏云：「宜以大臣鎮東道。」
units.en: When Lushan rose in rebellion, Yang Guozhong, wishing to curb Jinqing's standing at court, memorialized: "A senior minister should be posted to guard the eastern route."
units.literal: At the time when Lushan rebelled, Yang Guozhong because Jinqing had contemporary reputation intended to suppress him and memorialized saying: "It is fitting to have a great minister guard the eastern way."

units.zh: 廣德初，吐蕃寇長安。
units.en: Early in the Guangde era the Tibetans attacked Chang'an.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangde, the Tibetans raided Chang'an.

units.zh: 晉卿時病臥於私第，蕃聞之，輿入逼脅，晉卿閉口不言，賊不敢害。
units.en: Jinqing lay ill at home; the Tibetans heard of him, came in a litter to coerce him, but he kept silent and they did not dare harm him.
units.literal: Jinqing at the time lay ill in his private residence; the Tibetans heard of it, entered by litter to coerce him, Jinqing closed his mouth and did not speak, and the bandits did not dare harm him.

units.zh: 永泰元年四月薨。
units.en: He died in the fourth month of Yongtai 1 (765).
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongtai he died.

units.zh: 大歷七年，令配享肅宗廟庭。
units.en: In Dali 7 (772) he was ordered to share sacrifices in Suzong's temple.
units.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, he was ordered to share sacrifice in Suzong's temple court.

units.zh: 初授懷州修武縣尉，歷奉先縣尉，坐累貶徐州司戶參軍。
units.en: He was first made magistrate's assistant at Xiuwu in Huai, then served at Fengxian, but was demoted to registrar at Xu prefecture after being implicated in an affair.
units.literal: Initially appointed magistrate's assistant of Xiuwu County in Huai Prefecture, served as magistrate's assistant of Fengxian County, and because of entanglement in a case was demoted to Registrar of Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 秩滿隨調，判入高等，授萬年縣尉。
units.en: At the end of his term he entered the routine reassignment pool, scored in the top tier on his evaluation, and received appointment as assistant magistrate of Wannian.
units.literal: When his term ended he joined the regular transfer; his written evaluation was graded in the upper rank, and he was appointed magistrate's assistant of Wannian County.

units.zh: 晉卿性謙柔，選人有訴訟索好官者，雖至數千言，或聲色甚厲者，晉卿必含容之，略無慍色。
units.en: Jinqing was modest and even-tempered: when examinees petitioned or quarreled for better appointments, sometimes at great length or with angry outbursts, he always listened patiently and never showed annoyance.
units.literal: Jinqing's nature was modest and gentle; when candidates lodged complaints or sued for good posts, even if to several thousand words, or their voice and bearing were very fierce, Jinqing always bore with them, without a trace of anger.

units.zh: 李林甫為尚書，專任廟堂，銓事唯委晉卿及同列侍郎宋遙主之。
units.en: Li Linfu held the ministerial post but kept his grip on court power, leaving the actual running of selections to Jinqing and his fellow vice minister Song Yao alone.
units.literal: Li Linfu as Minister devoted himself solely to the court altar, and selection affairs were solely entrusted to Jinqing and his colleague Vice Minister Song Yao to preside.

units.zh: 上怒，晉卿貶為安康郡太守，遙為武當郡太守，張倚為淮陽太守。
units.en: The emperor's rage sent Jinqing to Ankang as prefect, Yao to Wudang, and Zhang Yi to Huaiyang.
units.literal: The Emperor was angry; Jinqing was demoted to Prefect of Ankang commandery, Yao to Prefect of Wudang commandery, Zhang Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang.

units.zh: 會入計，因上表請歸鄉里。
units.en: When he traveled to court for the annual account, he memorialized asking leave to revisit his home.
units.literal: When the occasion came to enter for the annual accounting, he therefore submitted a memorial requesting to return to his native place.

units.zh: 既至壺關，望縣門而步。
units.en: On reaching Huguan he dismounted and walked at the sight of the county gate.
units.literal: Having reached Huguan, he viewed the county gate and walked on foot.

units.zh: 晉卿曰：「《禮》：『下公門，式路馬。』
units.en: Jinqing replied: "The Rites say: 'When you leave a nobleman's gate, you bow to the horses on the road.'
units.literal: Jinqing said: "The Rites: 'When descending from the duke's gate, one salutes the road horses.'

units.zh: 況父母之邦，所宜尊敬。
units.en: How much more ought one to show reverence in the land of one's parents.
units.literal: How much more in the land of one's father and mother—what is fitting is reverence.

units.zh: 汝何言哉！」
units.en: What nonsense is that!"
units.literal: What words are you speaking!"

units.zh: 又俸錢三萬為鄉學本，以教授子弟。
units.en: He also endowed the local school with thirty thousand cash from his salary to teach the young men of the district.
units.literal: Again he took thirty thousand in salary cash as capital for a village school, to instruct the sons and younger brothers.

units.zh: 尋改河東太守、河東采訪使，入為尚書、東京留守，征為憲部尚書。
units.en: Soon after he was made prefect and investigating commissioner of Hedong, then minister and eastern capital guardian in the capital, and finally summoned as minister of justice.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Hedong Prefect and Hedong Investigating Commissioner, entered court as Minister and Eastern Capital Retention Officer, and was summoned as Minister of Justice.

units.zh: 遂出為陜州刺史、陜虢兩州防禦使。
units.en: He was therefore posted out as governor of Shaan and defense commissioner for Shaan and Guo.
units.literal: Thereupon he was sent out as Governor of Shaan Prefecture and Defense Commissioner of both Shaan and Guo prefectures.

units.zh: 及入對，固辭老病，由是忤旨，改憲部尚書致仕。
units.en: At audience he pleaded old age and illness and thereby offended the emperor, who stripped him of active duty and let him retire as titular minister of justice.
units.literal: When he entered to respond, he firmly declined on grounds of old age and illness; by this he offended the imperial will and was changed to Minister of Justice retiring from office.

units.zh: 及朝廷失守，衣冠流離道路，多為逆黨所脅，自陳希烈、張均已下數十人盡赴洛陽，晉卿潛遁山谷，南投金州。
units.en: When the capital fell, officials fled along the highways and many were forced into the rebels' ranks; dozens from Chen Xilie and Zhang Jun down went to Luoyang, but Jinqing hid in the hills and fled south to Jin prefecture.
units.literal: When the court lost its hold, caps and gowns wandered the roads, many were compelled by the rebel party—from Chen Xilie, Zhang Jun, and below, several tens all went to Luoyang; Jinqing secretly fled through mountain valleys and south cast himself to Jin Prefecture.

units.zh: 後以賊寇漸除，屢乞骸骨，優詔許之，罷知政事，為太子太傅。
units.en: As the rebels waned he repeatedly asked to retire; the throne graciously agreed, relieved him of government, and made him grand tutor to the heir apparent.
units.literal: Later because the bandit raiders were gradually eliminated, he repeatedly begged his old bones; a gracious edict permitted it, he ceased knowing administration, and became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 明年，帝思舊臣，復拜為侍中。
units.en: The following year the emperor recalled his veteran counselor and again appointed him palace attendant.
units.literal: The next year the emperor thought of old ministers and again appointed him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 性聰敏，達練事體，百司文簿，經目必曉，而修身守位，以智自全，議者比漢之胡廣。
units.en: He was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in affairs; once he had glanced at any document from the ministries he understood it, yet he cultivated himself and guarded his post, preserving himself by tact; critics compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.
units.literal: His nature was clever and keen; he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs—documents of the hundred offices, once passed before his eyes he necessarily understood them; yet he cultivated himself and guarded his position, preserving himself by wisdom; commentators compared him to Hu Guang of Han.

units.zh: 玄宗崩，肅宗詔晉卿攝冢宰。
units.en: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to serve as regent during the mourning.
units.literal: When Xuanzong died, Suzong ordered Jinqing to act as regent.

units.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞古者殷高宗在諒闇之中，百官聽於冢宰，更無事跡，但存文字。
units.en: He memorialized a firm refusal: "I have heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin mourned in seclusion, the hundred officials obeyed the regent—but we have no further record of actual governance from that time, only words on paper.
units.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining, saying: "Your servant has heard that in antiquity, when King Gaozong of Yin was in the period of deep mourning, the hundred officials listened to the regent—there are no further traces of affairs, only written records remain.

units.zh: 且一時之事，禮不相沿。
units.en: Moreover, that was a single occasion; ritual precedent does not bind every age.
units.literal: Moreover, affairs of a single time—rites do not follow one another.

units.zh: 今殘寇猶虞，日殷萬務，皆緣兵馬屯守討襲，善算良謀，立勝擒敵。
units.en: Today remnant rebels still threaten us and ten thousand affairs press in daily—all hinge on troops in the field, on sound strategy and swift victory over the enemy.
units.literal: Now remnant bandits still give concern; daily the myriad affairs press in—all depend on armies garrisoned, guarding, attacking, and striking; good calculation and fine plans to achieve immediate victory and capture the enemy.

units.zh: 陛下若行古之道，居喪不言，蒼生何依，百事皆廢。
units.en: If Your Majesty followed the ancient way and held mourning silence, what would become of the people? Every affair of state would collapse.
units.literal: If Your Majesty follows the ancient way, dwelling in mourning and not speaking, on what will the black-haired people rely? A hundred affairs will all be abandoned.

units.zh: 伏讀國家起居註，亦於禮部檢見舊敕，恭惟太宗、高宗、、大行皇帝在位之日，皆有國哀，視事不輟，以為君臨天下，難徇常情。
units.en: I have reverently read the court diary and old edicts in the Ministry of Rites: Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor, whenever the realm mourned, never ceased to govern, holding that a ruler of all under Heaven cannot indulge ordinary private feeling.
units.literal: Your servant has reverently read the national diary of activities and also in the Ministry of Rites examined old edicts; respectfully considering that in the days when Taizong, Gaozong, and the late emperor held the throne, whenever there was national mourning they did not cease attending to affairs, taking it that one who rules all under Heaven cannot follow ordinary sentiment.

units.zh: 今遺詔有處分，皇帝宜三日而聽政。
units.en: The late emperor's testament already directs that the new emperor should take up government after three days.
units.literal: Now the testamentary edict has provisions: the emperor ought on the third day to hear government.

units.zh: 陛下遵太宗故事，則無冢宰；
units.en: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, no regent is needed;
units.literal: If Your Majesty follows Taizong's precedent, then there is no regent;

units.zh: 遵大行皇帝遺詔，便合聽朝。
units.en: if you follow the late emperor's testament, you should take the throne at once.
units.literal: if you follow the late emperor's testamentary edict, then it is fitting at once to hear court.

units.zh: 萬姓颙颙，不勝大願。
units.en: The myriad people look up in hope with a longing that cannot be overstated.
units.literal: The myriad people look up in hope—they cannot bear their great wish.

units.zh: 伏惟陛下知理國之重，順人心之切，以義斷恩，從宜無改。
units.en: I trust Your Majesty knows how grave it is to govern the realm, how urgent the people's need is, and will set duty above private grief and do what the times require.
units.literal: Your servant considers that Your Majesty knows the weight of governing the state, follows the urgency of people's hearts, cuts off private feeling by righteousness, and follows what is fitting without change.

units.zh: 今朝臣一命已上，皆言臣心昏貌朽，加以疾病，事有急速，斷在須臾，凡聖不同，豈合受詔。
units.en: Every minister of the first rank and above says my mind is dim, my body worn, and my illness grave; urgent affairs are decided in an instant—a common man is no sage; how could I accept such a charge?
units.literal: Now court ministers of the first rank and above all say that your servant's mind is dim and his appearance decayed, with illness added; affairs of urgency are decided in a moment; ordinary and sage are not the same—how could it be fitting to receive the edict?

units.zh: 陛下發哀已五日矣，願準遺詔聽政，則四夷萬國，無任悲幸。」
units.en: Your Majesty has mourned five days already; I pray you follow the testament and take up government—the four quarters and all nations will be overwhelmed with grief and relief alike."
units.literal: Your Majesty has begun mourning for five days already; I wish you would follow the testamentary edict and hear government—then the four barbarians and ten thousand states will be unable to bear their grief and good fortune."

units.zh: 數日，肅宗晏駕，代宗踐祚，又詔晉卿攝冢宰。
units.en: Within days Suzong died and Daizong ascended the throne; he again ordered Jinqing to serve as regent.
units.literal: Several days later Suzong died; Daizong ascended the throne and again ordered Jinqing to act as regent.

units.zh: 晉卿上表懇辭曰：「臣以昔者天子居喪之時，百官聽於冢宰者，蓋君幼小，禦極事殷，情理當然。
units.en: Jinqing memorialized again in earnest refusal: "In former times, when the Son of Heaven mourned and officials obeyed a regent, it was because the ruler was a child and the throne's burdens were overwhelming—that was only natural.
units.literal: Jinqing submitted a memorial earnestly declining, saying: "Your servant considers that in former times when the Son of Heaven dwelt in mourning and the hundred officials listened to the regent, it was because the ruler was young and small, the throne's affairs were pressing—reason and sentiment made it natural.

units.zh: 沿革不一，今古異同，而周武、漢文，合於通變，垂範作則，可舉而行。
units.en: Custom has varied from age to age, yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han adapted wisely to circumstance and left examples we may follow.
units.literal: Change and continuation are not uniform; present and ancient differ in sameness and difference—yet King Wu of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Han conformed to flexible adaptation, handed down models and made standards that may be raised up and carried out.

units.zh: 又士或墨缞，時遇金革，豈非銜恤，謂義在斷恩。
units.en: A gentleman may wear mourning garb yet take up arms when the state is at war—he grieves inwardly but knows that duty must override private sorrow.
units.literal: Again, a gentleman may wear black hemp mourning, yet when the time meets arms and armor, is it not that he harbors grief yet holds that righteousness lies in cutting off private feeling?

units.zh: 且百善之至，無加於孝也，其有容瘁心絕，指景悼生，此匹夫守節之常情，殊王者嗣續之大計。
units.en: Filial piety is the highest of virtues, yet to waste away in grief and mourn one's own life is the conduct of a private man—not the great duty of one who must carry on the royal line.
units.literal: Moreover, among the hundred virtues none surpasses filial piety; yet there are those whose countenance is haggard and heart broken, who point to the sun and mourn life—this is the ordinary sentiment of a common man keeping integrity, quite different from the great plan of a king's succession.

units.zh: 昨二十日，陛下於大行皇帝柩前即位，是承先帝遺顧之言，亦前代不易之典。
units.en: Only yesterday, on the twentieth, Your Majesty took the throne before the late emperor's bier—fulfilling his final charge and following an immemorial precedent.
units.literal: Yesterday, the twentieth day, Your Majesty at the bier of the late emperor ascended the throne—this carries out the late emperor's parting charge and is also an unchanging canon of former ages.

units.zh: 則知所略不為害，所存是適權，防威滅端，所利者大。
units.en: What is set aside does no harm; what is preserved is timely expedience—cutting danger at the root brings the greater good.
units.literal: Then one knows that what is set aside does no harm and what is preserved is fitting expedience—warding off peril and extinguishing the source; the benefit is great.

units.zh: 陛下因心純至，天地明察。
units.en: Your Majesty's heart is utterly sincere; Heaven and Earth discern it.
units.literal: Your Majesty's heart follows purity to the utmost; Heaven and Earth see clearly.

units.zh: 伏以報劬勞之恩，申罔極之思，終身之痛，豈計朝夕！
units.en: To repay a parent's toil and express boundless grief is a lifelong sorrow—not a matter of days alone!
units.literal: Your servant considers that repaying toilsome labor's grace and expressing boundless longing—lifelong pain, how could one reckon by days and nights!

units.zh: 但以一日之內，萬務在中，須達宸聰，始成國政。
units.en: Yet within a single day ten thousand affairs press in; only when they reach Your Majesty's ear can the state be governed.
units.literal: Yet within a single day the myriad affairs lie at the center; the imperial ear must be reached before state government can be accomplished.

units.zh: 百僚萬姓及僧道耆壽等，相顧聚言，以臣老且無能，愚豈測聖，況久無居攝，臣不敢奉詔。
units.en: Officials, common people, monks, Daoists, and elders alike say I am old and incapable—how could a fool measure a sage? Regency has long been obsolete; I dare not accept the charge.
units.literal: The hundred officials, myriad people, monks and Daoists, elders of long years, and others look at one another and gather in speech, saying your servant is old and without ability—how could stupidity measure sagehood? Moreover, for long there has been no regency; your servant dares not accept the edict.

units.zh: 特乞陛下遵遺命，三日而政。
units.en: I beg Your Majesty only to follow the testament and take up government after three days.
units.literal: I specially beg Your Majesty to follow the testamentary command and govern after three days.

units.zh: 臣博聽眾情，不勝懇願，伏望割痛抑哀，則天下悲幸。」
units.en: Having heard the people's voice, I cannot state their wish strongly enough: I pray you set aside private grief, and the realm will be overwhelmed with sorrow and relief together."
units.literal: Your servant has broadly listened to the multitude's feelings and cannot bear the earnest wish; I bow and hope you will cut pain and restrain grief—then all under Heaven will be overwhelmed with grief and good fortune."

units.zh: 時晉卿年已衰暮，又患兩足，上特許肩輿至中書，入閣不趨，累日一視事。
units.en: Jinqing was then advanced in years and afflicted in both legs; the emperor specially allowed him a sedan chair to the Secretariat, exemption from hurrying into court, and attendance at affairs only every few days.
units.literal: At the time Jinqing's years were already declining in old age and he also suffered in both feet; the Emperor specially permitted him to be carried in a litter to the Secretariat, to enter the pavilion without hurrying, and to attend to affairs once every several days.

units.zh: 歷三朝，皆以謹密見稱。
units.en: Through three reigns he was praised for caution and discretion.
units.literal: Through three reigns he was in each case praised for caution and discretion.

units.zh: 及上自陜至，冊為太保，罷知政事，又詔以太保致仕。
units.en: When the emperor returned from Shaan, Jinqing was made grand guardian, relieved of government, and again ordered to retire with that title.
units.literal: When the Emperor came from Shaan, Jinqing was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, ceased knowing administration, and was again ordered to retire as Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 輟朝三日，令京兆少尹一員護喪事，緣葬諸物並官給，賻絹布五百段、米粟五百石。
units.en: Court mourning lasted three days; a junior capital official was assigned to oversee the funeral; all burial expenses were paid by the state, with five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain as condolence gifts.
units.literal: Court was suspended three days; one Junior Administrator of the Capital was ordered to oversee funeral affairs; all items connected with burial were supplied by the state; condolence gifts were five hundred lengths of silk and cloth and five hundred piculs of grain.

units.zh: 晉卿寬厚廉謹，為政舉大綱，不問小過，所到有惠化。
units.en: Jinqing was generous, upright, and discreet; in office he kept to broad principles and overlooked petty faults, and wherever he served he left a record of benevolent rule.
units.literal: Jinqing was generous, thick, honest, and cautious; in government he raised the great outline and did not inquire into small faults; wherever he arrived there was benevolent transformation.

units.zh: 初，晉卿東都留守，引用大理評事元載為推官。
units.en: Earlier, when Jinqing was eastern capital guardian, he had appointed Yuan Zai, an assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as his investigating officer.
units.literal: Earlier, when Jinqing was Eastern Capital Retention Officer, he brought in Yuan Zai, Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, as investigating officer.

units.zh: 陛下為撥亂主，今天下未平，李光弼在土門，來填在河南，魯炅在南陽，但留臣，臣以尺書招之，不日平矣。」
units.en: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian is in Henan, Lu Jiong in Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
units.literal: Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Jiong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."

units.zh: 作書招光弼等，諸將報書皆讓翰不死節。
units.en: He wrote to summon Guangbi and the others; every reply rebuked Han for failing to die with honor.
units.literal: He wrote letters to summon Guangbi and the others; the generals' replies all reproached Han for not dying in honor.

units.zh: 然暴橫少恩，杖前部尉以逞憾，觀察使王緯以聞，德宗不省。
units.en: Yet he was brutal and unforgiving: he had a former subordinate commandant flogged to settle a personal score. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported it, but Emperor Dezong paid no heed.
units.literal: Yet he was violent and overbearing and short on kindness; he beat a former subordinate commandant to vent a grudge. Observation commissioner Wang Wei reported this, but Emperor Dezong took no notice.

units.zh: 帝晚務姑息，頔所奏建，無不開允。
units.en: In his later years the emperor favored appeasement, and every proposal Di submitted won approval.
units.literal: The emperor in his later years pursued indulgence and forbearance; whatever Di memorialized and proposed was invariably approved.

units.zh: 俄擅以兵取鄧州，天子未始誰何。
units.en: Before long he seized Dengzhou by force on his own authority, and the emperor never called him to account.
units.literal: Soon he on his own authority took Dengzhou by force, and the Son of Heaven never once held him to account.

units.zh: 智興能駛步，奉表，不數日至京師告急，德宗出朔方軍五千擊納，解去，自是為徐特將。
units.en: Zhixing could run at great speed; he carried a memorial and reached the capital within days to report the crisis. Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuofang troops against Na and lifted the siege; from then on Zhixing was a special general of Xuzhou.
units.literal: Zhixing could run swiftly; he bore a memorial and in only a few days reached the capital to report the emergency. Dezong sent out five thousand Shuofang troops to strike Na, and the siege was lifted; from then on he was a special general of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 德宗既厭兵，大抵刺史重代易，至歷年不徙。
units.en: After the emperor wearied of campaigning, prefects were usually turned over often—though some lingered in office for years on end.
units.literal: Once Emperor Dezong grew weary of warfare, for the most part prefects were frequently rotated, yet some went years without transfer.

units.zh: 德宗立，召還。
units.en: Dezong's accession brought his recall to court.
units.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, he was recalled.

units.zh: 魏自崔亮以後。
units.en: In Northern Wei, since the time of Cui Liang,
units.literal: In Wei, since Cui Liang's time.

units.zh: 迺常以文部選才未為盡善，遂致書於知銓舍人宋昱曰：
units.en: Nai often felt that the Ministry of Personnel (Wenbu) did not select talent as well as it might, and wrote to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:
units.literal: Nai often considered that the Ministry of Personnel's selection of talent was not fully adequate and therefore sent a letter to Selection Attendant Song Yu, saying:

units.zh: 既終制，從調選曹。
units.en: When mourning ended, he went to the selection bureau for assignment.
units.literal: When mourning was complete, he followed the selection bureau for assignment.

units.zh: 於是劍南大擾，楊子琳起瀘州，與邛州柏貞節連和討寧。
units.en: Jiannan fell into chaos as Yang Zilin rose in Luzhou and joined Bai Zhenjie of Qiongzhou against Ning.
units.literal: Thereupon Jiannan was greatly disturbed; Yang Zilin rose from Lu Prefecture and joined with Bai Zhenjie of Qiong Prefecture to campaign against Ning.

units.zh: 乃表貞節為邛州刺史，子琳為瀘州刺史，以和解之。
units.en: He memorialized Zhenjie as prefect of Qiongzhou and Zilin as prefect of Luzhou to settle the feud.
units.literal: He then memorialized Zhenjie as Administrator of Qiong Prefecture and Zilin as Administrator of Lu Prefecture to make peace with them.

units.zh: 永泰元年，武卒。
units.en: In 765 Yan Wu died.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Wu died.

units.zh: 初，晏承旨，門下侍郎、同平章事王縉亦處極法，晏謂涵等曰：重刑再覆，國之常典，況誅大臣，得不覆奏？
units.en: When Yan first received the order, Vice Director Wang Jin was also slated for execution; Yan told Han and the others: 'Heavy sentences require double review—that is state law; in executing a great minister, must we not report back for confirmation?'
units.literal: At first, when Yan received the imperial directive, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Grand Councilor Wang Jin was also to receive the extreme penalty; Yan said to Han and the others: 'Heavy punishments require double review—this is the state's constant rule; moreover, in executing a great minister, must we not report back for confirmation?'

units.zh: 及晏等覆奏，代宗乃減縉罪從輕。
units.en: When Yan and the others reported back, Emperor Daizong lightened Jin's sentence.
units.literal: When Yan and the others reported back, Emperor Daizong reduced Jin's crime to a lighter punishment.

units.zh: 縉之生，晏平反之力也。
units.en: Jin owed his life to Yan's intervention.
units.literal: That Jin lived was due to Yan's effort to reverse the verdict.

units.zh: 以過從友人飲噱，為韋執誼密奏，貶虔州掾曹，復為考功員外郎裴垍善其應對機捷，遷考功郎中、集賢院學士，轉給事中。
units.en: He drank and jested too freely with friends; Wei Zhiyi secretly memorialized against him and he was demoted to a clerical post in Qianzhou. Later, as vice director of merit evaluation, he impressed Pei Ji with his quick wit and rose to director of merit evaluation, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and Drafting Attendant.
units.literal: For excessive drinking and jesting with friends he was secretly memorialized against by Wei Zhiyi and demoted to clerical officer of Qianzhou; later as vice director of merit evaluation, Pei Ji appreciated his quick and nimble responses and he was promoted to director of merit evaluation, academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and transferred to Drafting Attendant.

units.zh: 裴垍罷相，為太子賓客，未幾而卒。
units.en: When Pei Ji left office he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died soon after.
units.literal: When Pei Ji left the chancellorship he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent and died before long.

units.zh: 李吉甫復入相，與垍宿嫌，不加贈官；
units.en: When Li Jifu returned as chancellor, he bore an old grudge against Ji and granted no posthumous office;
units.literal: When Li Jifu returned to the chancellorship, he bore an old grudge against Ji and did not grant posthumous office;

units.zh: 伯芻上疏論之，贈垍太子少傅。
units.en: Boqu submitted a memorial on the matter, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: Boqu submitted a memorial arguing the point, and Ji was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 伯芻妻，垍從姨也。
units.en: Boqu's wife was Ji's maternal cousin.
units.literal: Boqu's wife was Ji's maternal cousin.
